newsitem.title: BRAZIL: No damaging cold this week for Brazil coffee - Somar.
newsitem.headline: No damaging cold this week for Brazil coffee - Somar.

text.p: Brazil's coffee regions should see no damaging cold over the coming seven days, with temperatures rising throughout the week, local meteorologists Somar said Sunday.

A polar air mass which passed swiftly through the south of the country this weekend led to cooler weather but lows in north Parana, the most southern coffee-growing region, were 10 to 12 degrees Celsius, said Somar forecaster Marcos Massari.

In the highland regions of Minas Gerais, temperatures should be at their coolest Sunday night/Monday morning because of clear skies but even so minimum temperatures were seen at around eight degrees Celsius, well above critical levels, he added.

Temperatures will pick up during the next seven days, with a second air mass which is to pass quickly through the far south of the country at the start of the week staying well clear of coffee regions.
